a maintenance biologic

Benlysta (belimumab) CMS Medicare Part D 2025, from the quarterly companion 4ff7c618 (Q1-Q4 2025): $291,468,828 over 7,431 beneficiaries = $39,223.37 per beneficiary. Why this comparator: no systemic Sjögren's therapy is marketed in the US, and Novartis itself calls ianalumab the potential first targeted treatment. Benlysta is the closest marketed match. It acts on the same BAFF pathway (it targets the ligand, ianalumab the receptor). It is prescribed by rheumatologists for SLE, the neighbouring systemic autoimmune disease. Its subcutaneous form is self-injected on the pharmacy benefit, as monthly 300 mg subcutaneous ianalumab will be (NCT06293365 tests its 2 mL autoinjector). The 2024 annual Part D figure was $37,182. Alternative: Benlysta Part B at $36,043.10 per beneficiary with a 0.056604 discount gives a net of $34,003, 73% above this net. Benlysta's mature per-beneficiary figure is used as is, not annualised.

column11: Capture identity from backend/capture_anchor.py (untreated convention), applied to Saphnelo, the last new biologic mechanism launched into a systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease. Saphnelo US revenue was $8m, $111m, $260m, $425m and $596m in 2021 to 2025 (AZ 20-F 0001104659-24-025553 and 0001104659-26-019130). The net price is $35,856 per patient-year (CMS Part B 2025: $38,007.17 per beneficiary x 1/1.06). That gives treated stocks of 223, 3,096, 7,251, 11,853 and 16,622. After 45.54% stop each year, new starts are 2,974, 5,565, 7,904 and 10,167. Against the untreated CDC SLE pool of 204,295, that is 1.46%, 2.77%, 4.04% and 5.42% (5.04% under the engine pool convention). 2025 is Saphnelo's fourth full year, which is 51.9% of the way up the fitted curve (k 0.31, midpoint 2.76). So the engine needs 10.45% to reproduce 5.42% at the same point. JUDGEMENT: multiple 0.75, giving 0.0784, which converts 4.07% of the untreated eligible pool in ianalumab's fourth year. Case for a higher multiple: it would be the first and only targeted Sjögren's therapy, while Saphnelo launched beside Benlysta. It is a monthly self-injection, not an IV. Two Phase 3s were positive and it has Breakthrough designation. The anchor is measured against all diagnosed SLE patients, not Saphnelo's narrower label pool, so it leans low. Case against: the placebo-adjusted ESSDAI gain was only -1.3 (NEPTUNUS-1, p=0.0496) and -1.0 (NEPTUNUS-2 monthly, p=0.041). The every-3-months arm failed (-0.5, p=0.34), and pooled patient-reported secondaries missed significance. ESSDAI must be scored for payers, and Maciel 2017 found community rheumatologists rarely run those tests. Crowded pool: dazodalibep follows in 2029, and nipocalimab (JNJ), deucravacitinib (BMY), telitacicept (VOR) and efgartigimod (argenx, readout July 2027) all have Sjögren's Phase 3s. None of them carries rows on indication 85 today. Pool crowding: pool_crowding.solve on indication:85 with dazodalibep rations no year (combined starts peak at 11.7% of the eligible pool). Counting the population once trims ianalumab's peak starts to 0.9348 of its standalone run.
